paragraphs.title: Faith Disturbed by the Success of the Wicked

answers: To Israel and those with a clean heart
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Truly God is good to Israel, even to such as are of a clean heart.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalm say that God is good?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.”
easy.q: At whom was the psalmist envious?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says they “speak wickedly concerning oppression” and “speak loftily.”

answers: Seeing the prosperity of the wicked
Losing his way in the wilderness
medium.explanation: He says his feet were almost gone because he was envious when he saw the prosperity of the wicked.
medium.q: What nearly caused the psalmist’s feet to slip?

answers: Violence was constantly part of their conduct
medium.explanation: The image shows that violence surrounded and characterized the wicked.
medium.q: What does “violence covereth them as a garment” suggest?

answers: Whether God knows and whether there is knowledge in the Most High
Whether the temple should be rebuilt
medium.explanation: They ask, “How doth God know? and is there knowledge in the most High?”
medium.q: What do the wicked question in verse 11?

answers: God is good to the pure in heart, yet the psalmist is troubled by the prosperity of the wicked
The wicked suffer while the righteous prosper
The psalmist abandons Israel to seek another land
challenge.explanation: The psalm begins with faith in God’s goodness but describes confusion caused by the wicked’s apparent success.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the opening section?

answers: They remain only in the sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The language pictures proud and defiant speech reaching both heaven and earth.
challenge.q: What does the statement that the wicked set their mouth against heaven and their tongue walk through the earth communicate?

answers: From confidence in God’s goodness to envy and concern over the wicked
From joy over the wicked to sorrow for the righteous
From denying God to worshipping idols
challenge.explanation: The section moves from the declaration that God is good to the psalmist’s struggle with the wicked’s prosperity and pride.
challenge.q: How does the psalmist’s attitude develop in verses 1–12?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Person’s Doubts and Understanding in the Sanctuary

easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “Verily I have cleansed my heart in vain.”
easy.q: What did the psalmist think about cleansing his heart?

easy.explanation: Verse 14 says, “For all the day long have I been plagued.”
easy.q: What did the psalmist experience all day long?

answers: That the wicked would prosper forever
easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “Then understood I their end.”
easy.q: What did the psalmist understand when he entered the sanctuary of God?

medium.explanation: In the sanctuary, he gained spiritual understanding of the wicked’s end.
medium.q: What led the psalmist to understand the fate of the wicked?

answers: Their position was unstable and led to downfall
medium.explanation: The image of slippery places points to instability and sudden destruction.
medium.q: What does it mean that God set the wicked in slippery places?

medium.explanation: Verse 20 compares their appearance to “a dream when one awaketh.”
medium.q: To what is the apparent prosperity of the wicked compared?

answers: They appear prosperous now, but their end is sudden destruction
They suffer now, but later receive riches
challenge.explanation: Although they seem secure, the psalmist learns that they will be brought into desolation and destruction.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the wicked’s present appearance and their final end?

answers: He feared offending the generation of God’s children
The wicked had forbidden him to speak
challenge.explanation: He says that speaking in that way would offend “the generation of thy children.”
challenge.q: Why did the psalmist hesitate to speak openly about his doubts?

challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the final outcome and judgment of the wicked.
challenge.q: What does “their end” mean in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Recognizing Human Limits and Relying on God

answers: It was filled with earthly joy
easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “Thus my heart was grieved.”
easy.q: What happened to the psalmist’s heart?

easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “Thou hast holden me by my right hand.”
easy.q: By which hand did God hold the psalmist?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou shalt guide me with thy counsel, and afterward receive me to glory.”
easy.q: What would God do afterward, according to verse 24?

answers: He lacked understanding of God’s ways
medium.explanation: He admits that he did not understand the situation and was spiritually ignorant.
medium.q: What does the psalmist mean by saying he was foolish and ignorant?

answers: God remains with him, holds him, guides him, and receives him to glory
God abandons him and leaves him without counsel
The psalmist becomes independent of God
medium.explanation: These verses present God’s continual presence, support, guidance, and final reception.
medium.q: What sequence is described in verses 23–24?

answers: His grief and lack of understanding
medium.explanation: His grief and confession of foolishness show that he recognizes his own limitations.
medium.q: What led the psalmist to recognize his limitations?

answers: The psalmist’s recognition that he lacked understanding
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes his inability to understand God’s ways.
challenge.q: What does the comparison to a beast before God express?

answers: A movement from recognizing human limits to relying on God’s guidance
A movement from pride to denying God
A movement from honor to fear
challenge.explanation: The psalmist admits that he does not understand, then trusts God to guide him.
challenge.q: What change is shown between being ignorant and being guided by God’s counsel?

answers: Grief and confession of ignorance, followed by God’s presence, guidance, and glory
challenge.explanation: The verses move from the psalmist’s painful realization to confidence in God’s continual guidance.
challenge.q: What is the overall progression of this section?

paragraphs.title: Closeness to God as the Greatest Good

easy.explanation: Verse 25 says, “Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.”
easy.q: Who is the psalmist’s greatest desire?

easy.explanation: Verse 26 says, “My flesh and my heart faileth.”
easy.q: What happens to the psalmist’s flesh and heart?

easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “It is good for me to draw near to God.”
easy.q: What is it good for the psalmist to do?

answers: God is the psalmist’s lasting inheritance and possession
The psalmist will receive earthly riches
The psalmist will rule over nations
medium.explanation: The phrase means that God is the psalmist’s enduring source and inheritance.
medium.q: What does “my portion for ever” mean in this passage?

answers: Those far from God perish, while the psalmist finds good in drawing near to Him
Those far from God receive honor, while the psalmist is destroyed
medium.explanation: Verse 27 speaks of the destruction of those far from God, while verse 28 affirms the goodness of nearness to Him.
medium.q: What contrast is made between those far from God and the psalmist?

medium.explanation: He says he trusts in the Lord GOD “that I may declare all thy works.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist intend to do because he has put his trust in the Lord GOD?

answers: God as the strength of his heart and his portion for ever
challenge.explanation: Verse 26 identifies God as the strength of his heart and his eternal portion.
challenge.q: What remains constant when the psalmist’s flesh and heart fail?

answers: As drawing near to God, trusting Him, and declaring His works
As gaining wealth and worldly honor
challenge.explanation: The final verses connect goodness with nearness to God, trust, and testimony.
challenge.q: How does this section define true goodness?

answers: Trust in God gives the psalmist a reason and confidence to tell of His works
Trust causes the psalmist to remain silent
Declaring God’s works replaces trust in Him
challenge.explanation: Because God is his refuge, the psalmist is moved to declare all that God has done.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between trusting God and declaring His works?
